title: Dispatch fragmentation SLO investigation
content:
Summary:

This note captures the investigation into intermittent tail-latency SLO violations we observed in October–December 2025 that correlate with long-context MoE workloads (Llama/Mistral/Qwen mixes). The failure mode is unusual: median latency is stable, but p95/p99 spikes by 3–6x under moderate load (50–70% cluster utilization) for requests with windows > 8k tokens. The pattern points to dispatch/fragmentation of expert fanout and small, misaligned batch fragments hitting serialization and I/O hot paths.

Why this doc exists:
- Capture reproducible repro steps and traces
- Enumerate root-cause hypotheses and evidence
- Track mitigation experiments and short-term patches
- Propose longer-term scheduler/serialization changes with cost/complexity trade-offs

Observed symptom set (summary of runs):
- Workloads: mixed-model traffic using MoE-enabled variants of Llama-70b, Mistral-22b-MoE, and Qwen-34b-MoE. Typical input: long-context system prompts (2–10k tokens) + user history (2–6k tokens).
- Env: Dedicated G5x2 pools (32GB HBM), runtime release: r2025-11-13 (kernel fusion + new prefetch), routing config: dynamic top-k gating (k=2) with session affinity turned on.
- Behavior: p50 stable (~120ms per token); p95 and p99 show burst spikes when concurrent sessions with diverse requested experts overlap. Spikes occur even at moderate throughput (150–200 tokens/s per GPU).
- Notable trace characteristic: dispatch fragments of size <= 8 tokens (very small micro-batches) appear in the same RL/worker window as large fragments (~256 tokens). Small fragments incur scheduling/serialization overhead and cause cross-host synchronization stalls.

Key evidence collected:
1) Perf traces (perf + eBPF hooks) show serialization queues growing on the worker handing off to expert hosts. When a worker has to send 8 small fanouts to 8 experts sequentially (instead of coalesced), the sum of RPC latencies dominates.
2) Flamegraphs from local profiling show two hotspots: (a) rpc_send_serialized (copy+pack) and (b) expert-handshake-wait. The copy+pack cost is disproportionately high for small fragments because of repeated header overhead.
3) Network traces show many tiny gRPC frames (overhead per frame ~0.9ms). Aggregating the same payload into single frames saves 60–80% of the observed overhead in microbenchmarks.
4) KV cache behavior: long-context requests cause large KV footprints, which push many expert cache entries to the UVM eviction path. This increases serialization churn because workers try to prefetch missing KV shards while simultaneously dispatching small fragments.
5) Model-level observation: Mistral-MoE gating produces higher variance in expert selection across the same batch compared to Llama-MoE (we think due to gating temperature hyperparameters). That increases the chance of minimal overlap and hence fragmentation.

Root-cause hypotheses (ranked):
A) Dispatch fragmentation: gating + diverse sessions create many small, non-coalesced fanouts that hit RPC and serialization overhead at scale. (High confidence)
B) IO serialization path not optimized for sub-32-token fragments: repeated buffer copies and header assembly dominate when fragment sizes are tiny. (High confidence)
C) KV cache prefetch interference: prefetch/evict operations block dispatch worker or generate extra small RPCs. (Medium confidence)
D) Per-expert backpressure misaccounting: scheduler allows too many fragmented requests to accumulate on the same flow, creating head-of-line stalls. (Medium confidence)
E) Model-architecture gating dynamics: Qwen/Mistral gating patterns produce more skew and less coalescence than Llama; this amplifies A/B/C. (Low→Medium confidence)

Repro recipe (minimal):
1) Use dedicated dev pool: gpu-dev-g5x2-12 (region-us-west2).
2) Runtime snapshot: r2025-11-13 with routing flags --gating=dynamic --affinity=on.
3) Workload generator script: ./tools/gen_moe_mix.sh --models llama70,qwen34,mistral22 --sessions 400 --window 12k --mean_user_hist 3k --qps 6. Attach to slack thread ts-1700000000 for the script version.
4) Collector: enable trace-level=rpc+dispatch+kv (10s windows), sampled traces at 1/200.

Microbenchmarks we ran (high-level numbers):
- Coalesced payload (256 tokens combined into single RPC) median = 1.8ms, p99 = 3.5ms
- Non-coalesced 8-token fragments (8 frames instead of 1) median = 9.1ms, p99 = 23.8ms
- Prefetch disabled: fragmentation spikes reduced by ~12% but memory stalls increased.
- Buffer-copy optimized (local patch) for small payloads: reduced p99 on microbench by ~35%.

Short-term mitigations tried (ranked by rollout priority):
1) RPC coalescing heuristic (canary): coalesce all fragments <= 32 tokens destined for the same expert into a single outgoing frame within a 1ms batching window. Result: p99 improved by 30% in canary; delicate for real-time SLOs. PR: runtime/pull/2789.
2) Small-fragment fast-path: avoid repeated header copies by reusing preallocated buffer for fragments < 16 tokens. Result: local microbench p99 drop 20–40%.
3) Lower gating temperature for Mistral variant in canary to increase expert overlap. Result: better coalescence but slight quality regression on edge prompts. Needs eval gating.
4) Prefetch back-off policy: if worker detects high fragmentation, deprioritize prefetch (reduces eviction churn). Result: mixed; reduced dispatch stalls but increased KV miss rate slightly.

Risks/observations for rollouts:
- Coalescing introduces a bounded delay (1ms window) that affects worst-case latency for single-token low-latency requests. We need per-route configuration to avoid harming low-token SLOs.
- Prefetch back-off can increase token compute time when missing; must be combined with coalescing for net gain.
- Model-level gating tweaks need quantitative evals (use existing eval harness: CON-REG-2025-09).

Longer-term design options (cost/complexity):
1) Smarter coalescing in router: maintain in-flight fragment buckets per expert per worker and attempt deterministic coalescing using adaptive windows driven by traffic variance. (Complexity: medium; rollback-friendly)
2) Change serialization protocol: switch to length-prefixed vectors that avoid per-frame header copies for small fragments. Requires cross-team coordination (runtime + network layer). (Complexity: high; high benefit)
3) Per-expert microqueue schedulers: allow reordering/coalescing across multiple workers before RPC dispatch (introduces centralization; complexity high).
4) Gating-aware placement: prefer expert placement that increases physical locality for frequently co-occurring experts in long-context sessions. (Cost: may require rebalancing and warm-up periods).
5) KV cache sharding improvements: ensure prefetch does not block dispatch path, e.g., make prefetch async with separate worker threads and better backpressure signals. (Complexity: medium)

Immediate next steps (action items):
- [Aisha] Merge and dogfood PR runtime/pull/2789 to a small dedicated Canary (target: 2026-02-10). Track p95/p99 over 2 weeks.
- [Miguel] Run gating-temperature eval sweep on Mistral/Qwen combo with our eval harness (CON-REG-2025-09) and produce trade-off slide. (target: 2026-02-17)
- [Jordan] Prototype serialization format change for small-fragment fast-path (spike only; no rollout). Collect microbench numbers. (target: 2026-03-01)
- [Priya] Investigate KV prefetch back-off signal design and coordinate with infra to measure eviction stall impact. (target: 2026-02-24)

Open questions / discussion points:
- Is 1ms coalescing window acceptable for web-tier pluggable functions routes? Suggest per-route opt-in default: coalescing_enabled=false for routes with expected token size < 8.
- Do we want to expose gating temperature control as a runtime override per-customer? Ops and security implications to pricing.
- Long-term: do we accept complexity of per-expert microqueue vs. protocol-level serialization improvements? Which aligns better with Dedicated and Private deployment maintenance surface?

Appendix (short logs and sample trace snippets):
- Trace excerpt (worker W23, t=2025-11-07T03:12:09Z):
  * dispatch: create fragments [8,256,16,8,128] -> rpc_send_serialized x5 -> avg rpc frame time 0.84ms -> total dispatch overhead 15.2ms -> expert-handshake-wait adds 10.6ms.
- Microbench script reference: tools/micro_coalesce_bench.py --payload 32 --fragments 8 --repeat 2000

If you want to reproduce quickly, ping me in #runtime-performance; I'll share the workload generator and can open a small dev Canary for any of the proposed patches.
